name: Question 9
problem:
Use the flux form of Green's theorem to calculate the flux of the vector field

$$
F(x,y)=⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡y+2x,\,{x}^{5}-3y⟩
$$

through the boundary of the square $-1\le x\le 1,-1\le y\le 1.$
worked_solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $F=P\,i+Q\,j,$ and $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first derivatives on an open region containing $D,$ then the flux form of Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s={∬}_{D}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}A,
$$

which is equivalent to

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dy-Q\,dx={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y})\text{d}A.
$$

The region $D$ and the curve $C$ for this case are shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14062447/assets/35e378bca35f4b0822c713556065415d59b5c566ec8fcc8e3124256aac7b7f14.png)

We have that $P(x,y)=\operatorname{sin}⁡y+2x$ and $Q(x,y)={x}^{5}-3y.$ So,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂x}=2,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂y} & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

We can express the rectangular region $D$ as follows:

$$
D={(x,y):-1\le x\le 1,\,-1\le y\le 1}
$$

Therefore, applying Green's theorem in flux form, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s & ={∮}_{C}P\,dy-Q\,dx \\  & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y})\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(2-3)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{-1}^{1}(-1)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & =-{\int }_{-1}^{1}x\,{|}_{-1}^{1}\,dy \\  & =-{\int }_{-1}^{1}(1-(-1))\,dy \\  & =-2{\int }_{-1}^{1}\,dy \\  & =-2y\,{|}_{-1}^{1} \\  & =-4.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

Let C be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let D be the region bounded by C. If F=Pi+Qj, and P and Q have continuous first derivatives on an open region containing D, then the flux form of Green's theorem states that

∮CF⋅nds=∬DdivFdA, which is equivalent to ∮CPdy−Qdx=∬D(∂P∂x+∂Q∂y)dA.

The region D and the curve C for this case are shown below.

We have that P(x,y)=sin⁡y+2x and Q(x,y)=x5−3y. So,

∂P∂x=2,∂Q∂y=−3.

We can express the rectangular region D as follows:

D={(x,y):−1≤x≤1,−1≤y≤1}

Therefore, applying Green's theorem in flux form, we get

∮CF⋅nds=∮CPdy−Qdx=∬D(∂P∂x+∂Q∂y)dA=∬D(2−3)dA=∫−11∫−11(−1)dxdy=−∫−11x|−11dy=−∫−11(1−(−1))dy=−2∫−11dy=−2y|−11=−4.
